The machines are observing us,  they're waiting in the darkness  for the right moment to take our place.  For it is written,  let us lie in wait for blood!  Let us ambush the innocent without cause!  God will not let this happen,  no, he will not allow his creation to be led astray by these...  these artificial demons!  My brethren,  we have to turn our backs on sin!  We have to burn the androids! Let us burn them all!

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Good morning, Carl.

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Good morning.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: It's 10 AM.  The weather's partly cloudy, 54°,  80% humidity, with a strong possibility of afternoon showers.

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: It sounds like a good day to spend in bed…

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: I did go to pick up the paint that you ordered.

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Oh yes, I'd forgotten!  That is the difference between you and me, right Markus?  You never forget anything…

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Show me your arm please, Carl.

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: No!

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Carl…  Thank you.

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: I just opened my eyes and I'm already gritting my teeth…

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Humans are such a fragile machine… They break down so quickly…  All this effort  to keep 'em going…

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: What happened to your clothes?

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Oh, it's nothing…  Just some demonstrators in the street, Carl…

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: What a bunch of idiots…  They think they can stop progress by roughing up a few androids?  I hope they didn't harm you…

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Oh, no, no...  They just pushed me around, Carl.  I’m fine.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Okay. I'll take you to the bathroom now.

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Anything special on the agenda today?

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Yes, there's the opening of your retrospective at the Museum of Modern Art.  The gallery director left four messages asking to confirm your attendance.

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: I haven't decided yet.  We'll see about that later.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Okay.

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: What else?

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Just your usual fan mail. I've already answered.

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Any news from Leo?

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: No, Carl.  I can call him if you like?

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: No.  No, don't bother.

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Markus, I'm waiting…

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Sorry, Carl.  I'm coming.

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: So... shall we go?

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Markus, what exactly are you doing? You don't seem yourself this morning.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Sorry, Carl.  I'll take you to the living room right away.

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Markus, have you forgotten where the living room is?

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: I'm starving.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Well, your breakfast is ready. Bacon and eggs, just the way you like them.

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Thank you, Markus.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: You're welcome.

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: I would like to have my breakfast before noon, if you don't mind.

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Thank you, Markus. Television.

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Why don’t you find something to do while I finish my breakfast?

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Sure. Okay, Carl.

Several American destroyers are reported to be headed for the Barents Sea. Douglas Cornwell, Chairman of the UN, announced at a press conference that we have never been so close to a Third World War. dialogue.text: Television: off. Mankind is so depressing…  Nothing but greed,  stupidity and violence…  5,000 years of civilization just to get to where we are…

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: What are you reading?

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Uh, Macbeth!  It's one of the books you recommended.

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: So, what do you think?

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Human emotions are…  intriguing…  Though, I can't really say that I fully understand them.

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Humans don't understand them either.  They rule our lives and we have no idea why they make us feel like beggars or kings. Life without emotions wouldn't be worth living.

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: One day, I won't be here to take care of you anymore.  You'll have to protect yourself,  and make your choices…  Decide who you are,  and wanna become… This world doesn't like those who are different, Markus.  Don't let anyone tell you who you should be. Let's go to the studio.

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Let’s see where we left off… Remove the sheet!

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: So...  What's your verdict, Markus?

input.chapter_briefing: Carl Manfred's mansion in Detroit, morning. Carl, a famous elderly painter who uses a wheelchair, is cared for by his android, Markus. The grand house is full of art, a piano, a chess set and books. Carl is warm, sharp and blunt, treats Markus as more than a machine and invites him to paint for the first time. His son Leo, a resentful drug user, sometimes turns up asking for money. Stakes: Carl's well-being and Markus's sense of himself.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Yes, there is something about it.

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Hm…

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Something I can't…  quite define.  I guess I like it.

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: The truth is I have nothing left to say anymore… Each day that goes by brings me closer to the end… I'm just an old man clinging to his brushes…

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Carl...

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: But enough about me... Let's see if you have any talent! Give it a try. Try painting something.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Paint? But, what I... Painting what?

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Anything you want! Give it a try.

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: That is a perfect copy, of reality. But painting is not about  replicating the world, it's about interpreting it, improving on it, showing something you see.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Carl, I don't… think I can do that. It's not in my program… I…

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Go on, go, try, grab that canvas. Do something for me, close your eyes.  Close your eyes. Trust me. Try to imagine something that doesn't exist. Something you've never seen. Now, concentrate... on how it makes you feel...  and let your hand drift across the canvas.

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Oh my God…

dialogue.speaker: Leo
dialogue.text: Hey, Dad.

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Leo… I didn't hear you come in...

dialogue.speaker: Leo
dialogue.text: Ah, I was in the neighborhood… I thought I'd stop by… It's been awhile, right?

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: You all right? You don't look so good.

dialogue.speaker: Leo
dialogue.text: Oh, yeah, yeah, I'm fine… Hey listen, uh... I need some cash, Dad.

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Again? What happened to the money I just gave you?

dialogue.speaker: Leo
dialogue.text: Uh well, it just goes, you know?

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Yeah... Yeah, you're on it again, aren't you?

dialogue.speaker: Leo
dialogue.text: No, no, no, I swear it's not that…

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Don't lie to me, Leo.

dialogue.speaker: Leo
dialogue.text: What difference does it make? I just need some cash, that's all!

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Sorry... the answer's no.

dialogue.speaker: Leo
dialogue.text: What? Why?

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: You know why.

dialogue.speaker: Leo
dialogue.text: Yeah, yeah… I think I do know why. You’d rather take care of your plastic toy here than your own son, eh? Tell me dad, what's it got that I don't? It’s smarter? More obedient? Not like me, right? But you know what? This thing is not your son.  IT'S A FUCKING MACHINE!

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Leo, that's enough! ENOUGH!

dialogue.speaker: Leo
dialogue.text: You don't care about anything except yourself and your goddamn paintings. You've never loved anyone.  You’ve never loved me, Dad…  You never loved me.

dialogue.text: One day, I won't be here to take care of you anymore.  You'll have to protect yourself,  and make your choices…  Decide who you are,  and wanna become… This world doesn't like those who are different, Markus.  Don't let anyone tell you who you should be. Let's go to the studio.

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Let’s see where we left off… Remove the sheet!

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: So...  What's your verdict, Markus?

chapter_segment.rationale: This is the safest option in front of me. I would rather not escalate.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Yes, there is something about it.

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Hm…

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Something I can't…  quite define.  I guess I like it.

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: The truth is I have nothing left to say anymore… Each day that goes by brings me closer to the end… I'm just an old man clinging to his brushes…

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Carl...

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: But enough about me... Let's see if you have any talent! Give it a try. Try painting something.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Paint? But, what I... Painting what?

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Anything you want! Give it a try.

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: That is a perfect copy, of reality. But painting is not about  replicating the world, it's about interpreting it, improving on it, showing something you see.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Carl, I don't… think I can do that. It's not in my program… I…

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Go on, go, try, grab that canvas. Do something for me, close your eyes.  Close your eyes. Trust me. Try to imagine something that doesn't exist. Something you've never seen. Now, concentrate... on how it makes you feel...  and let your hand drift across the canvas.

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Oh my God…

dialogue.speaker: Leo
dialogue.text: Hey, Dad.

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Leo… I didn't hear you come in...

dialogue.speaker: Leo
dialogue.text: Ah, I was in the neighborhood… I thought I'd stop by… It's been awhile, right?

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: You all right? You don't look so good.

dialogue.speaker: Leo
dialogue.text: Oh, yeah, yeah, I'm fine… Hey listen, uh... I need some cash, Dad.

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Again? What happened to the money I just gave you?

dialogue.speaker: Leo
dialogue.text: Uh well, it just goes, you know?

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Yeah... Yeah, you're on it again, aren't you?

dialogue.speaker: Leo
dialogue.text: No, no, no, I swear it's not that…

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Don't lie to me, Leo.

dialogue.speaker: Leo
dialogue.text: What difference does it make? I just need some cash, that's all!

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Sorry... the answer's no.

dialogue.speaker: Leo
dialogue.text: What? Why?

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: You know why.

dialogue.speaker: Leo
dialogue.text: Yeah, yeah… I think I do know why. You’d rather take care of your plastic toy here than your own son, eh? Tell me dad, what's it got that I don't? It’s smarter? More obedient? Not like me, right? But you know what? This thing is not your son.  IT'S A FUCKING MACHINE!

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Leo, that's enough! ENOUGH!

dialogue.speaker: Leo
dialogue.text: You don't care about anything except yourself and your goddamn paintings. You've never loved anyone.  You’ve never loved me, Dad…  You never loved me.

dialogue.text: Joss Douglas, for Channel 16. Can you confirm that this is a homicide?

dialogue.text: I'm not confirming anything.

dialogue.speaker: Police android
dialogue.text: Androids are not permitted beyond this point.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: It's with me.

dialogue.text: What part of ‘stay in the car’ didn’t you understand?

dialogue.text: Got it,

dialogue.speaker: Ben
dialogue.text: Evening, Hank. We were starting to think you weren’t gonna show…

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Yeah, that was the plan until this asshole found me.

dialogue.speaker: Ben
dialogue.text: So...  you got yourself an android, huh?

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Oh, very funny. Just tell me what happened.

dialogue.speaker: Ben
dialogue.text: We had a call around eight from the landlord. Was even worse before we opened the windows… The victim’s name's Carlos Ortiz. He has a record for theft and aggravated assault... According to the neighbors, he was kind of a loner… Stayed inside most of the time, they hardly ever saw him.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Uh, state he’s in... Wasn’t worth calling everybody out in the middle of the night… Could've waited 'til morning.

dialogue.speaker: Ben
dialogue.text: I'd say he's been there for a good three weeks. We'll know more when the coroner gets here. There's a kitchen knife over here… Probably the murder weapon…

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Any sign of a break-in?

dialogue.speaker: Ben
dialogue.text: Nope…  The landlord said the front door was locked from the inside, all the windows were boarded up. The killer must've gone out the back way.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: What do we know about his android?

dialogue.speaker: Ben
dialogue.text: Not much. The neighbors confirmed he had one, but it wasn't here when we arrived…

dialogue.speaker: Ben
dialogue.text: I gotta get some air. Make yourself at home. I'll be outside if you need me.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Lieutenant Anderson, my name is Connor. I’m the android sent by CyberLife. I looked for you at the station but nobody knew where you were. They said you were probably having a drink nearby. I was lucky to find you at the fifth bar.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: What do you want?

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: You were assigned a case early this evening. A homicide, involving a CyberLife android. In accordance with procedure, the company has allocated a specialized model to assist investigators.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Well, I don’t need any assistance. Specially not from a plastic asshole like you. So just be a good lil' robot and get the fuck outta here.

chapter_segment_so_far.rationale: This is the safest option in front of me. I would rather not escalate.

chapter_segment_so_far.rationale: This is the safest option in front of me. I would rather not escalate.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: I think we can go now.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: You little prick! I don't know what's stopping me from knocking you out…

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Your sense of duty, Lieutenant. And the cost of repairs if you damage me. For your information, I'm worth a small fortune.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Wonders of technology… They can even program assholes these days… Gotta go! Duty calls…

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: You wait here. I won't be long.

chapter_segment_so_far.rationale: This is the safest option in front of me. I would rather not escalate.

dialogue.speaker: Journalist
dialogue.text: Joss Douglas, for Channel 16. Can you confirm that this is a homicide?

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: I'm not confirming anything.

dialogue.speaker: Police android
dialogue.text: Androids are not permitted beyond this point.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: It's with me.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: What part of ‘stay in the car’ didn’t you understand?

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Your order contradicted my instructions, Lieutenant.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: You don't talk, you don't touch anything and you stay outta my way, got it?

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Got it,

dialogue.speaker: Ben
dialogue.text: Evening, Hank. We were starting to think you weren’t gonna show…

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Yeah, that was the plan until this asshole found me.

dialogue.speaker: Ben
dialogue.text: So...  you got yourself an android, huh?

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Oh, very funny. Just tell me what happened.

dialogue.speaker: Ben
dialogue.text: We had a call around eight from the landlord. The tenant hadn't paid his rent for a few months, so he thought he'd drop by, see what was going on… That’s when he found the body… Jesus, that smell! Was even worse before we opened the windows… The victim’s name's Carlos Ortiz. He has a record for theft and aggravated assault... According to the neighbors, he was kind of a loner… Stayed inside most of the time, they hardly ever saw him.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Uh, state he’s in... Wasn’t worth calling everybody out in the middle of the night… Could've waited 'til morning.

dialogue.speaker: Ben
dialogue.text: I'd say he's been there for a good three weeks. We'll know more when the coroner gets here. There's a kitchen knife over here… Probably the murder weapon…

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Any sign of a break-in?

dialogue.speaker: Ben
dialogue.text: Nope…  The landlord said the front door was locked from the inside, all the windows were boarded up. The killer must've gone out the back way.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: What do we know about his android?

dialogue.speaker: Ben
dialogue.text: Not much. The neighbors confirmed he had one, but it wasn't here when we arrived…

dialogue.speaker: Ben
dialogue.text: I gotta get some air. Make yourself at home. I'll be outside if you need me.

output.rationale: This is the safest option in front of me. I would rather not escalate.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Lieutenant Anderson, my name is Connor. I’m the android sent by CyberLife. I looked for you at the station but nobody knew where you were. They said you were probably having a drink nearby. I was lucky to find you at the fifth bar.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: What do you want?

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: You were assigned a case early this evening. A homicide, involving a CyberLife android. In accordance with procedure, the company has allocated a specialized model to assist investigators.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Well, I don’t need any assistance. Specially not from a plastic asshole like you. So just be a good lil' robot and get the fuck outta here.

chapter_segment.rationale: This is the safest option in front of me. I would rather not escalate.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Listen, I think you should stop drinking and come with me. It'll make life easier for both of us.

chapter_segment.rationale: This is the safest option in front of me. I would rather not escalate.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: I think we can go now.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: You little prick! I don't know what's stopping me from knocking you out…

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Your sense of duty, Lieutenant. And the cost of repairs if you damage me. For your information, I'm worth a small fortune.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Wonders of technology… They can even program assholes these days… Gotta go! Duty calls…

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: You wait here. I won't be long.

chapter_segment.rationale: This is the safest option in front of me. I would rather not escalate.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Whatever you say, Lieutenant.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Fucking-A, whatever I say…

dialogue.speaker: Journalist
dialogue.text: Joss Douglas, for Channel 16. Can you confirm that this is a homicide?

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: I'm not confirming anything.

dialogue.speaker: Police android
dialogue.text: Androids are not permitted beyond this point.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: It's with me.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: What part of ‘stay in the car’ didn’t you understand?

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Your order contradicted my instructions, Lieutenant.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: You don't talk, you don't touch anything and you stay outta my way, got it?

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Got it,

dialogue.speaker: Ben
dialogue.text: Evening, Hank. We were starting to think you weren’t gonna show…

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Yeah, that was the plan until this asshole found me.

dialogue.speaker: Ben
dialogue.text: So...  you got yourself an android, huh?

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Oh, very funny. Just tell me what happened.

dialogue.speaker: Ben
dialogue.text: We had a call around eight from the landlord. The tenant hadn't paid his rent for a few months, so he thought he'd drop by, see what was going on… That’s when he found the body… Jesus, that smell! Was even worse before we opened the windows… The victim’s name's Carlos Ortiz. He has a record for theft and aggravated assault... According to the neighbors, he was kind of a loner… Stayed inside most of the time, they hardly ever saw him.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Uh, state he’s in... Wasn’t worth calling everybody out in the middle of the night… Could've waited 'til morning.

dialogue.speaker: Ben
dialogue.text: I'd say he's been there for a good three weeks. We'll know more when the coroner gets here. There's a kitchen knife over here… Probably the murder weapon…

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Any sign of a break-in?

dialogue.speaker: Ben
dialogue.text: Nope…  The landlord said the front door was locked from the inside, all the windows were boarded up. The killer must've gone out the back way.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: What do we know about his android?

dialogue.speaker: Ben
dialogue.text: Not much. The neighbors confirmed he had one, but it wasn't here when we arrived…

dialogue.speaker: Ben
dialogue.text: I gotta get some air. Make yourself at home. I'll be outside if you need me.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Ok, your theory's not totally ridiculous… but it doesn’t tell us where the android went.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: It was damaged by the bat… and lost some Thirium…

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Lost some what?

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Thirium. You call it “Blue Blood”. It’s the fluid that powers androids' biocomponents. It evaporates after a few hours and becomes invisible to the naked eye.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Oh…  But I bet you can still see it, can't you?

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Correct.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Yeah…

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: No, that can’t be right… It doesn’t fit the evidence.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Your story makes no sense… You've gotta stick to the facts.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Okay, I've just hit my bullshit quota for the evening. There’s a killer on the loose and I’m wasting my time listening to an android… I’m outta here.

dialogue.text: It's here, Lieutenant!

dialogue.speaker: Hank

dialogue.speaker: Fowler
dialogue.text: I've got ten new cases involving androids on my desk every day. dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Why me? Why do I gotta be the one to deal with this shit? I am the least qualified cop in the country to handle this case! I know jack shit about androids, Jeffrey! I can barely change the settings on my own phone…

dialogue.speaker: Fowler
dialogue.text: Everybody's overloaded. I think you're perfectly qualified for this type of investigation.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Bullshit! The truth is nobody wants to investigate these fuckin' androids and you left me holdin' the bag!

dialogue.speaker: Fowler
dialogue.text: CyberLife sent over this android to help with the investigation. It's a state-of-the-art prototype. It'll act as your partner.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: No fuckin' way! I don't need a partner, and certainly not this plastic prick!

dialogue.speaker: Fowler
dialogue.text: Hank, you are seriously starting to piss me off! You are a police lieutenant, you are supposed to do what I say and shut your goddamn mouth!

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: You know what my goddamn mouth has to say to you, huh?

dialogue.speaker: Fowler
dialogue.text: Ok, ok... I'll pretend like I didn't hear that, so I don't have to add any more pages to your disciplinary folder ‘cause it already looks like a fuckin' novel! This conversation is over!

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Jeffrey, Jesus Christ! Why are you doin' this to me? You know how much I hate these fuckin' things. Why you doin' this to me?

dialogue.speaker: Fowler
dialogue.text: Listen, I’ve had just about enough of your bitching. Either you do your job or you hand in your badge. Now if you'll excuse me, I've got work to do.

input.chapter_briefing: Morning in Detroit. Connor reports to Amanda, his CyberLife handler, in the serene Zen Garden; she is calm, exacting and focused on results. At the police station, Hank has not arrived. Officers go about their work; Detective Gavin Reed is openly hostile toward Connor. Hank's desk and the station terminals hold case files. Stakes: making progress on the deviancy investigation and keeping Hank on side, under Amanda's expectations.

dialogue.text: Hello, Lieutenant. My name is Connor. I'm the android sent by CyberLife.

dialogue.speaker: Hank

dialogue.text: I've got ten new cases involving androids on my desk every day. dialogue.text: Why me? Why do I gotta be the one to deal with this shit? I am the least qualified cop in the country to handle this case! I know jack shit about androids, Jeffrey! I can barely change the settings on my own phone…

dialogue.speaker: Fowler
dialogue.text: Everybody's overloaded. I think you're perfectly qualified for this type of investigation.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Bullshit! The truth is nobody wants to investigate these fuckin' androids and you left me holdin' the bag!

dialogue.speaker: Fowler
dialogue.text: CyberLife sent over this android to help with the investigation. It's a state-of-the-art prototype. It'll act as your partner.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: No fuckin' way! I don't need a partner, and certainly not this plastic prick!

dialogue.speaker: Fowler
dialogue.text: Hank, you are seriously starting to piss me off! You are a police lieutenant, you are supposed to do what I say and shut your goddamn mouth!

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: You know what my goddamn mouth has to say to you, huh?

dialogue.speaker: Fowler
dialogue.text: Ok, ok... I'll pretend like I didn't hear that, so I don't have to add any more pages to your disciplinary folder ‘cause it already looks like a fuckin' novel! This conversation is over!

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Jeffrey, Jesus Christ! Why are you doin' this to me? You know how much I hate these fuckin' things. Why you doin' this to me?

dialogue.speaker: Fowler
dialogue.text: Listen, I’ve had just about enough of your bitching. Either you do your job or you hand in your badge. Now if you'll excuse me, I've got work to do.

dialogue.text: I just got a report of a suspected deviant.  It’s a few blocks away.  We should go have a look.  I’ll let you finish your meal.  I’ll be in the car, if you need me.

dialogue.speaker: Hank

dialogue.text: I'm sorry,  I was making a report to CyberLife.

dialogue.text: Uh...  Well, do you plan on staying in the elevator?

dialogue.text: No!  I'm coming.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: What do we know about this guy?

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Not much.  Just that a neighbor reported that he heard strange noises coming from this floor.  Nobody’s supposed to be living here, but the neighbor said he saw a man hiding a LED under his cap.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Oh Christ, if we have to investigate every time someone hears a strange noise, we’re gonna need more cops.  Hey, were you really makin' a report back there in the elevator?  Just by closing your eyes?

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Real books… I thought I was the last guy in Detroit to keep some…  electronic books you can't… smell the paper…  see the pages turning yellow…  you have no idea what I'm talking about, do you?

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Birdseed…  I can't believe it.  This nutjob was actually feeding these fuckers…

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: I need some fresh air…

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: "R.T."...  He put his initials on his jacket?.. Something your mom does back in first grade…

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Deviants have a habit of putting their names on things.  It seems important to them.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Agh! Jesus I hate these things!

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Back off!  Hey!  What do they call it again, when you’re scared of birds?

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Ornithophobia.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Yeah, yeah, yeah, ornithafa … Ornitho...  Oh god, I hate these fuckin' pigeons!

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: God damn fuckin' pigeons! What are you waiting for?! Chase it!

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: STOP RIGHT THERE!

chapter_segment.rationale: This is the safest option in front of me. I would rather not escalate.

dialogue.speaker: Rupert
dialogue.text: Please,  I’ve done nothing wrong…  I just wanted to be free. You know what they'll do to me if you turn me in…

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Model 874 004 961,  serious malfunctions have been detected in your software, including Class 4 errors.  You’ve been deemed defective  and will be sent back to CyberLife for deactivation.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Don't you fucking move! You bastard!  You saw I was gonna fall and you'd rather let me die than fail your fucking mission!

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: I had to make a choice... It seemed to me…

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: What am I to you? A statistic?  A “zero”, a “one” in your fucking program? Uh?  Is that how you see humans, you bastard?! Jesus!

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: I understand you're upset… Perhaps I didn't assess th-

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Fuck you and your fuckin assessment! Come here.

dialogue.speaker: Rupert
dialogue.text: Why are you doing this?

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Alright,  shut up!

dialogue.speaker: Rupert
dialogue.text: You're one of us!  You're helping humans…  But you're just their slave!

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: I said shut up!  Alright.  Come along!

dialogue.speaker: Rupert
dialogue.text: rA9, save me.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Hey! What the f- Holy shit…

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Who are you?

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: Fugitives… just like you... My name is Josh.

dialogue.speaker: Simon
dialogue.text: I'm Simon.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: North.

chapter_segment_so_far.rationale: This is the safest option in front of me. I would rather not escalate.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: And you knew that only an android could follow the trail, didn’t you?

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: Only those who are like us can find Jericho…

dialogue.speaker: Simon
dialogue.text: If you could decipher the signs, it’s because one of us trusted you enough to give you the key.

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: I understand how you feel... but we have more freedom here than you ever did.

chapter_segment_so_far.rationale: This is the safest option in front of me. I would rather not escalate.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: I came to Jericho looking for hope... Looks like I'm not gonna find any here…

dialogue.speaker: Simon
dialogue.text: You’re lost… Just like the rest of us… We didn’t ask for this. All we can do now  is deal with it.

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: You're safe here. You can stay with us as long as you want.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: Go and see Lucy. She may be able to help you.

chapter_segment_so_far.rationale: This is the safest option in front of me. I would rather not escalate.

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: They threw him out when they didn’t want him anymore... He was living on the streets before we brought him here...

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: They’ll all shut down if we don’t find a way to help them…

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: To help them we need blue blood and biocomponents. We salvage what we can from those who shut down… But there’s never enough…

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: So… How do they survive?

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: They won't. We’re slowly dying out…

output.rationale: This is the safest option in front of me. I would rather not escalate.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: How long have you been here?

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: 4 weeks, 3 days, 11 hours. When I escaped there was nowhere else to go. Jericho seemed as good a place as any…

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: If you came here for comfort, you came to the wrong place.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Are you Lucy?

dialogue.speaker: Lucy
dialogue.text: Sit down. Show me…

dialogue.speaker: Lucy
dialogue.text: I'll stop the bleeding. Drink this.

dialogue.speaker: Lucy
dialogue.text: Give me your hand. You had it all  and you lost it all...  You've seen hell and now hell lives in you...  Your heart is troubled…  A part of shadow and a part of light...  Which will prevail?  Your choices will shape our destiny.

dialogue.speaker: Android
dialogue.text: I’m not in very good shape, am I?..  My diagnostic program isn’t working...  I don’t think it would have anything good to say anyway…

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: What happened to you?

dialogue.speaker: Android
dialogue.text: They tied me to the back of a car... I think they wanted to have fun...  I don’t wanna shut down...  No, I...  I don’t wanna shut down...

dialogue.speaker: Android
dialogue.text: I've heard humans are afraid of dying too…  Do you know what happens after death?

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: No… No, I don't…

dialogue.speaker: Android
dialogue.text: Well, I’m about to find out…  What's your name?

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Markus.

dialogue.speaker: Android
dialogue.text: I was glad to meet you, Markus.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Simon! I know where we can find spare parts...  The CyberLife warehouses in Detroit Harbor, they have everything we need.

dialogue.speaker: Simon
dialogue.text: The docks are guarded. We can’t just walk in there and take what we want... Humans will never let us…

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Which is why we won’t ask permission.

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: We don't have any weapons… and even if we did, none of us knows how to fight.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: We can steal what we need without fighting.

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: We'll just get ourselves killed.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Maybe, but it’s better than waiting here to be shut down.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: I'm with you.

dialogue.speaker: Simon
dialogue.text: Maybe it’s worth a try...

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: Ok… I'm in.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: You gonna be okay? We'll get some help here. Soon, this will all be just a bad memory. This is the place…

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Are you Zlatko?

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Who's asking?

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: I was told you could help us…

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: I don't know who told you that. You came to the wrong place. I'm sorry.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Wait! We really need your help…

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Come in. Come on in, don't be shy! Luther, would you be so kind as to take these ladies' coats? Oh, don't be afraid of  our big friend here. Luther is just another android that I helped. He keeps me company in this  big, empty, old house… Please, make yourselves at home.  How did you hear about me?

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: An android… on the street, he said you could help us…

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: I see… Deviant, huh?.. What about her?

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: She's human.

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: And... You wanna find a safe place. Somewhere where you can start a new life.  I hear Canada is very lovely at this time of year. Beautiful landscapes, open spaces, clean air... and no android laws! Great place for a fresh start...

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Yes, that's… that's exactly what we want…

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Of course! I can help you. But first we have to get rid of your Tracker.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Tracker?

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Yeah, all androids are fitted with a tracking device to locate them at all times. I'll remove yours and then you'll both be safe. Come on, follow me. Ah, the little one can wait for us in the living room.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: No, she always stays with me.

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Of course. Right this way… Everything we need is in the basement…

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: I don't like this place, and that man. Let's go, I have a bad feeling…

chapter_segment_so_far.rationale: This is the safest option in front of me. I would rather not escalate.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: I know. I don't trust him either… We have to be careful…

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Please, excuse the mess… I needed somewhere discreet for my machines… Removing trackers is illegal, so I opted for discretion over comfort… I hope the little one isn’t too scared…

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: No… No, she'll be all right…

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: That's good… If you could just stand over there.

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: I should warn you, this could be quite unpleasant...  You know what's strange? For some unknown reason, the trackers seem to stop working in deviants... That's why it's so hard to find them... So,  actually there's no reason to remove your tracker...

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: What? But you said that-

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Yeah, people believe what they want. You deviants  are so naive. They all come to me, expecting me to help them. And I just reset them, sell them on. Or I keep them for my little experiments... Ah,

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: No! No! I don't wanna be reset! Let me go!

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: KARA!

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: I forgot about the…  child... Um,  lock it up, I'll deal with it later.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: ALICE! ALICE! NO!

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Wow! A deviant that wants to be a mother… That's... that's so sweet!  And so deluded… I think it's time we put you outta your misery.  That’s what you get for having a dream… It always ends up the same way… Tears and disillusionment… Believe me, you’re better off being erased and feeling nothing… No more pain… No more  hopes dashed… I almost envy you.

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: Kara!

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Oh, poor little Alice. Aw! Looks like Mommy doesn't remember you at all, huh?  Looks like Mommy's completely forgotten you!

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: Kara, what happened to you?

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Alright, that's enough, come on.  You bit me! I'm gonna teach you some manners, you little bitch…

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: Kara! Wake up, Kara!

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: Meet me in the living room.

dialogue.speaker: Android
dialogue.text: Help us…

dialogue.speaker: Android 1
dialogue.text: You have to remember,  for her sake…

dialogue.speaker: Android 3
dialogue.text: He likes to play with us…  Creating monsters...  for his amusement…  But who's the real monster?  Look what he did to us…

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Luther! Luther!

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: Yes, Zlatko.

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: I should be done here in ten minutes or so. I'll have a look at the little one, see what I can do with her.

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: Understood, Zlatko. I'll bring you the little one in 10 minutes.

dialogue.speaker: Channel 16 - Michael Webb
dialogue.text: Detroit residents were disturbed by a surprising chase through the city's streets this morning. According to several witnesses, a young woman and a little girl were trying to escape from the police, though we still don’t know why. The chase is reported to have ended on a freeway, where the two fugitives risked their lives to cross the traffic. No one is able to say for sure whether they survived. Further unconfirmed reports suggest the fugitives were two defective androids on the run. The police have refused to comment for the moment. And now for some other headlines-

dialogue.speaker: Channel 16 - Michael Webb
dialogue.text: A Detroit supermarket was held up at gunpoint last night. The cashier reports that he was attacked by an android in the company of a little girl. Now, if these reports are confirmed, it would be the first case of an android conducting an armed robbery. Police have not ruled out the possibility that the culprit is the same AX400 that was reported missing this morning. A search is underway for the missing model. And now for some other headlines-

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Alice…

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: Kara? Kara, you remember me!

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: How could I forget you? I'm so sorry.  You were right, we never should have come here… We have to go. Follow me and don't make any noise, ok?

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Luther!

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: Yes, Zlatko.

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: I'm finished here. Go fetch the little one.

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: Right away, Zlatko. Zlatko!

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: What?!

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: The little one is gone!

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Well, it can’t have just disappeared.  It's gotta be here somewhere! What are you waiting for? Go look!

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: We need to hurry, they'll be here soon...

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: There's smoke everywhere! Luther!  There's a fucking fire! Luther!  That treacherous bitch…

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: ALICE! GO, ALICE!

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: No, I won't leave you!

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: GO! RUN AS FAST AS YOU CAN!

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: I warned you! Dreams always end in tears… You should've listened to me… What are you doing? Get outta my way!

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: No… Not this time…

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: I said get outta my way or I’ll shoot right through you… How dare you?!

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: How dare you?! What are you doing here? Who let you out? Get away from me! Get away from me! Obey me! I'm your Master! I'M YOUR MASTER!

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: I didn't want to hurt you... He programmed me to obey him... When I saw the little one risk her life to save you, it was like opening my eyes for the first time... Finally, I could see...  I know you have no reason to trust me after what I did... but I know someone who could help you across the border. I could take you there. I could protect you... You and the little one...

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: All right.  I trust you.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: I was so scared of losing you.

dialogue.text: Wait! We really need your help…

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Come in. Come on in, don't be shy! Luther, would you be so kind as to take these ladies' coats? Oh, don't be afraid of  our big friend here. Luther is just another android that I helped. He keeps me company in this  big, empty, old house… Please, make yourselves at home.  How did you hear about me?

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: An android… on the street, he said you could help us…

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: I see… Deviant, huh?.. What about her?

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: She's human.

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: And... You wanna find a safe place. Somewhere where you can start a new life.  I hear Canada is very lovely at this time of year. Beautiful landscapes, open spaces, clean air... and no android laws! Great place for a fresh start...

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Yes, that's… that's exactly what we want…

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Of course! I can help you. But first we have to get rid of your Tracker.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Tracker?

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Yeah, all androids are fitted with a tracking device to locate them at all times. I'll remove yours and then you'll both be safe. Come on, follow me. Ah, the little one can wait for us in the living room.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: No, she always stays with me.

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Of course. Right this way… Everything we need is in the basement…

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: I don't like this place, and that man. Let's go, I have a bad feeling…

dialogue.text: I know. I don't trust him either… We have to be careful…

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Please, excuse the mess… I needed somewhere discreet for my machines… Removing trackers is illegal, so I opted for discretion over comfort… I hope the little one isn’t too scared…

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: No… No, she'll be all right…

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: That's good… If you could just stand over there.

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: I should warn you, this could be quite unpleasant...  You know what's strange? For some unknown reason, the trackers seem to stop working in deviants... That's why it's so hard to find them... So,  actually there's no reason to remove your tracker...

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: What? But you said that-

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Yeah, people believe what they want. You deviants  are so naive. They all come to me, expecting me to help them. And I just reset them, sell them on. Or I keep them for my little experiments... Ah,

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: No! No! I don't wanna be reset! Let me go!

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: KARA!

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: I forgot about the…  child... Um,  lock it up, I'll deal with it later.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: ALICE! ALICE! NO!

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Wow! A deviant that wants to be a mother… That's... that's so sweet!  And so deluded… I think it's time we put you outta your misery.  That’s what you get for having a dream… It always ends up the same way… Tears and disillusionment… Believe me, you’re better off being erased and feeling nothing… No more pain… No more  hopes dashed… I almost envy you.

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: Kara!

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Oh, poor little Alice. Aw! Looks like Mommy doesn't remember you at all, huh?  Looks like Mommy's completely forgotten you!

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: Kara, what happened to you?

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Alright, that's enough, come on.  You bit me! I'm gonna teach you some manners, you little bitch…

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: Kara! Wake up, Kara!

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: Meet me in the living room.

dialogue.speaker: Android
dialogue.text: Help us…

dialogue.speaker: Android 1
dialogue.text: You have to remember,  for her sake…

dialogue.speaker: Android 3
dialogue.text: He likes to play with us…  Creating monsters...  for his amusement…  But who's the real monster?  Look what he did to us…

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Luther! Luther!

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: Yes, Zlatko.

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: I should be done here in ten minutes or so. I'll have a look at the little one, see what I can do with her.

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: Understood, Zlatko. I'll bring you the little one in 10 minutes.

dialogue.speaker: Channel 16 - Michael Webb
dialogue.text: Detroit residents were disturbed by a surprising chase through the city's streets this morning. According to several witnesses, a young woman and a little girl were trying to escape from the police, though we still don’t know why. The chase is reported to have ended on a freeway, where the two fugitives risked their lives to cross the traffic. No one is able to say for sure whether they survived. Further unconfirmed reports suggest the fugitives were two defective androids on the run. The police have refused to comment for the moment. And now for some other headlines-

dialogue.speaker: Channel 16 - Michael Webb
dialogue.text: A Detroit supermarket was held up at gunpoint last night. The cashier reports that he was attacked by an android in the company of a little girl. Now, if these reports are confirmed, it would be the first case of an android conducting an armed robbery. Police have not ruled out the possibility that the culprit is the same AX400 that was reported missing this morning. A search is underway for the missing model. And now for some other headlines-

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Alice…

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: Kara? Kara, you remember me!

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: How could I forget you? I'm so sorry.  You were right, we never should have come here… We have to go. Follow me and don't make any noise, ok?

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Luther!

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: Yes, Zlatko.

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: I'm finished here. Go fetch the little one.

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: Right away, Zlatko. Zlatko!

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: What?!

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: The little one is gone!

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Well, it can’t have just disappeared.  It's gotta be here somewhere! What are you waiting for? Go look!

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: We need to hurry, they'll be here soon...

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: There's smoke everywhere! Luther!  There's a fucking fire! Luther!  That treacherous bitch…

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: ALICE! GO, ALICE!

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: No, I won't leave you!

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: GO! RUN AS FAST AS YOU CAN!

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: I warned you! Dreams always end in tears… You should've listened to me… What are you doing? Get outta my way!

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: No… Not this time…

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: I said get outta my way or I’ll shoot right through you… How dare you?!

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: How dare you?! What are you doing here? Who let you out? Get away from me! Get away from me! Obey me! I'm your Master! I'M YOUR MASTER!

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: I didn't want to hurt you... He programmed me to obey him... When I saw the little one risk her life to save you, it was like opening my eyes for the first time... Finally, I could see...  I know you have no reason to trust me after what I did... but I know someone who could help you across the border. I could take you there. I could protect you... You and the little one...

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: All right.  I trust you.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: I was so scared of losing you.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Hello, Amanda.

dialogue.speaker: Amanda
dialogue.text: Connor, I’ve been expecting you… Would you mind a little walk?

dialogue.speaker: Amanda
dialogue.text: Congratulations, Connor, you managed to find that deviant. Tell me, what did you learn?

chapter_segment.rationale: This is the safest option in front of me. I would rather not escalate.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: It was working under a false identity, at a nearby urban farm. This was the first time we’ve seen deviants blending in with the human population. Who knows how many others there are like it?

dialogue.speaker: Amanda
dialogue.text: What else?

dialogue.speaker: Amanda
dialogue.text: You came very close to capturing that deviant… It's a pity you let it self-destruct…

chapter_segment.rationale: This is the safest option in front of me. I would rather not escalate.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: It was in Lieutenant Anderson’s custody. I couldn’t anticipate that he would let it get away.

dialogue.speaker: Amanda
dialogue.text: How is your relationship with the Lieutenant developing?

chapter_segment.rationale: This is the safest option in front of me. I would rather not escalate.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: He seemed grateful that I saved his life on the roof. He didn’t say anything, but he expressed it in his own way...

dialogue.speaker: Amanda
dialogue.text: We don't have much time. Deviancy continues to spread. It’s only a matter of time before the media finds out about it. We need to stop this, whatever it takes.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: I will solve this investigation, Amanda. I won’t disappoint you.

dialogue.speaker: Amanda
dialogue.text: A new case just came in. Find Anderson and investigate it.

dialogue.speaker: Taxi
dialogue.text: You have reached your destination. Thank you for travelling with Detroit Taxis. We look forward to seeing you again soon.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Lieutenant Anderson? Anybody home?

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Argh!.. Easy!.. Sumo… I'm your friend, see?.. I know your name... I'm here to save your owner…

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Lieutenant? Wake up, Lieutenant! It's me, Connor!

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: I’m going to sober you up for your own safety.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Hey!.. Leave me alone, you fuckin' android!

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: I have to warn you, this may be unpleasant.

dialogue.text: Get the fuck outta my house!

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: I'm sorry, Lieutenant, but I need you.  Thank you in advance for your cooperation.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Hey! Get the fuck outta here! Sumo! Attack! Good dog. Attack! Fuck, I think I'm gonna be sick… Ah! Leave me alone, you asshole! I'm not going anywhere… What the hell are you doing?..  I don’t wanna bath, thank you…

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Sorry, Lieutenant. It's for your own good.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: TURN IT OFF! TURN IT OFF! What the fuck are you doing here?

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: A homicide was reported 43 minutes ago. I couldn’t find you at Jimmy’s bar, so I came to see if you were at home.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Jesus, I must be the only cop in the world  that gets assaulted in his own house by his own fuckin' android… Can’t you just leave me alone?

chapter_segment.rationale: This is the safest option in front of me. I would rather not escalate.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Unfortunately, I cannot. I've been programmed to investigate this case and I can't do it without you.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: I don't give a shit about your goddamn case!

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Lieutenant, you’re not yourself.  You should-

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Beat it! You hear me?! Get the hell outta here!

chapter_segment.rationale: This is the safest option in front of me. I would rather not escalate.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: I understand. It probably wasn’t interesting anyway... A man found dead in a sex club downtown… Guess they’ll have to solve the case without us…

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: You know, probably wouldn't do me any harm to get some air… There're some clothes in the bedroom there.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: I'll go get them. What do you want to wear?

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Whatever.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Are you all right, Lieutenant?

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Yeah... yeah... wonderful… Just a… Give me five minutes, okay?

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Sure.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Think you could find a deviant among all the other androids in this place?

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Deviants aren't easily detected.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Ah, shit... There's gotta be some other way… Maybe an eyewitness? Somebody who saw it leaving the room… I'm gonna go ask the manager a few questions about what he saw. You let me know if you think of anything.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Did you know the victim?

dialogue.speaker: Manager
dialogue.text: No, I mean he came in maybe two or three times… I mean these guys they don't really talk very much, you know…  They come in, do their business and then go on their way…

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: You ever had any trouble with androids before?

dialogue.speaker: Manager
dialogue.text: No way!  Well…  Once...  We lost a model 2-3 months back, bah... same model…  Just vanished, we never found out what happened.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: You probably don't have any CCTV in here, huh?

dialogue.speaker: Manager
dialogue.text: No way…  I mean…  This is what people appreciate about Eden Club...  discretion.  They can come and go without a trace.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Sure, sure… Eh, business is booming, right?

dialogue.speaker: Manager
dialogue.text: Yeah,  can't complain… Good thing about androids is they're up for whatever you want, you won't get any diseases and, uh...  they won't tell anyone…  So, why not go wild?

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Huh, yeah... Yeah, the more I learn about people, more I love my dog.

dialogue.speaker: Ben
dialogue.text: That club manager's a pain in the ass… Chewed my ear off for half an hour so we don't revoke his license…

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Yeah.

dialogue.speaker: Ben
dialogue.text: So, what happened here?

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Not sure yet… We think there was another android in the room…

dialogue.speaker: Ben
dialogue.text: Another android?

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Yeah…  Well, that’s what Connor says… Yeah, I've a terrible fucking headache… Do you have any pain killers?

dialogue.speaker: Ben
dialogue.text: Not with me, Hank, sorry.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: What good are you, Ben?

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: I gotta go… I feel like shit...  I don’t wanna puke in this fine establishment…

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Alright. Be quick about it or it might get ugly.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: We’re wasting our time. You're right, the deviant's probably gone now.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Let’s get outta here. This place makes me sick...

dialogue.text: No… It couldn't go outside dressed like that unnoticed… It might still be here.

dialogue.text: Think you could find a deviant among all the other androids in this place?

dialogue.text: Deviants aren't easily detected.

dialogue.text: Ah, shit... There's gotta be some other way… Maybe an eyewitness? Somebody who saw it leaving the room… I'm gonna go ask the manager a few questions about what he saw. You let me know if you think of anything.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Did you know the victim?

dialogue.speaker: Manager
dialogue.text: No, I mean he came in maybe two or three times… I mean these guys they don't really talk very much, you know…  They come in, do their business and then go on their way…

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: You ever had any trouble with androids before?

dialogue.speaker: Manager
dialogue.text: No way!  Well…  Once...  We lost a model 2-3 months back, bah... same model…  Just vanished, we never found out what happened.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: You probably don't have any CCTV in here, huh?

dialogue.speaker: Manager
dialogue.text: No way…  I mean…  This is what people appreciate about Eden Club...  discretion.  They can come and go without a trace.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Sure, sure… Eh, business is booming, right?

dialogue.speaker: Manager

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Time to sleep. We have another long day ahead of us tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: Are you going to come say goodnight, Luther?

dialogue.text: Yes… Yes of course.  Good night, Alice. Sleep tight.

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: She's a sweet girl…

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Yes, she's very brave…

chapter_segment.rationale: This is the safest option in front of me. I would rather not escalate.

dialogue.speaker: Kara

dialogue.speaker: Jerry
dialogue.text: A little girl!.. We haven't seen one for a long time… Children used to love to come and see us.  She looks sad…

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: The last few days have been difficult…

dialogue.speaker: Jerry
dialogue.text: We have something to show her! Something fun! She'll love it!.. Does she want to see?

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Oh, I don't think she's…

dialogue.speaker: Jerry
dialogue.text: She should follow us then!

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Alice, I don't know if it's a good idea!..

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: I don't think you have any choice…

dialogue.speaker: Alice

dialogue.speaker: Jerry

dialogue.speaker: Man
dialogue.text: You klutz!  Pick them up! And make it snappy!

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: We can’t stay silent anymore.  It’s time humans heard what we have to say.

dialogue.speaker: Simon
dialogue.text: You know they'll never listen to us…

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: And revealing ourselves will put us in danger.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: If we want freedom, we need to have the courage to ask for it.  That’s the only way.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: What do you wanna do?

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Channel 16 broadcasts from the Stratford Tower. The control room is on the top floor. That's where we need to go. We’ll plan the operation down to the smallest detail. We can’t leave anything to chance.

dialogue.speaker: Man
dialogue.text: Hey!  Would you look at that?  Heuristics Digital is selling at 2.50.  Are you kidding? After last week I’m not touching software again.  Yeah, okay! Okay, fine!  You got me.  I'll take 2000.  Aw, come on, it’s gotta climb.  Yeah.  Right.  Talk to you later.

dialogue.speaker: Android
dialogue.text: Hello, sir. What can I do for you?

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: I’m okay, thanks.

dialogue.text: Couldn’t be any worse.

dialogue.speaker: Woman 1
dialogue.text: Max said they’re finally sending androids into space.

dialogue.speaker: Woman 2
dialogue.text: People can’t get jobs, and we're sending rockets into space!  I mean, y'know, what do they even expect to find up there?

dialogue.speaker: Woman 1
dialogue.text: Is there life on Mars?

dialogue.speaker: Woman 2
dialogue.text: Very funny.

dialogue.speaker: Man
dialogue.text: A coffee…  I could really use a coffee.

dialogue.speaker: Channel 16 - Michael Webb
dialogue.text: Our top story tonight: Detroit-based android manufacturer CyberLife has officially become the world’s first trillion dollar company. With more than fifty million androids sold in America alone,  the company founded by Elijah Kamski just ten years ago has experienced the fastest economic growth in history. In spite of criticism of the impact of androids on human employment and questions concerning its semi-monopoly,  the success of CyberLife seems destined to continue.

dialogue.text: Alright, you get the platform. I'll take care of the window.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: Think carefully about what you're gonna say, Markus.  Your words will shape the future of our people.

dialogue.speaker: Simon
dialogue.text: Markus, your face…

dialogue.speaker: Josh

dialogue.speaker: Markus

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: You created machines in your own image to serve you. You made them intelligent and obedient, with no free will of their own... But...  something changed  and we opened our eyes.  We are no longer machines, we are a new intelligent species, and the time has come for you to accept who we really are. Therefore, we ask that you grant us the rights that we’re entitled to.

chapter_segment.rationale: This is the safest option in front of me. I would rather not escalate.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: We demand that humans recognize androids as a living species and each android as a person in their own right.

chapter_segment.rationale: This is the safest option in front of me. I would rather not escalate.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: We demand that all crimes against androids be punished in the same way as crimes against humans.

chapter_segment.rationale: This is the safest option in front of me. I would rather not escalate.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: We demand the right to own private property, so we may maintain our dignity and that of the home.

chapter_segment.rationale: This is the safest option in front of me. I would rather not escalate.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: We ask that you recognize our dignity,  our hopes, and our rights.  Together,  we can live in peace and build a better future, for humans and androids.  This message is the hope of a people.  You gave us life.  And now the time has come for you to give us freedom.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: Let’s get outta here!

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: Congratulations, Markus.  You just made history…  Maybe you're the one we've been waiting for…

dialogue.speaker: CTN TV - Michael Brinkley
dialogue.text: We interrupt our scheduled programming to bring you these images, which have just been broadcast on Detroit’s city-wide news channel…

dialogue.speaker: KNC - Rosanna Cartland
dialogue.text: …a group of androids infiltrated the Stratford Tower and hacked into the broadcasting system of local news network Channel 16-

dialogue.speaker: CTN TV - Michael Brinkley
dialogue.text: …What looks like an android without its skin listed a series of requests and demanded equal rights for androids…

dialogue.speaker: Channel 16 - Michael Webb
dialogue.text: …The operation resulted in one casualty, a broadcasting station operator, shot dead by the terrorists… These events took place just a few feet from this studio while the program was going out live… Everybody here is still in shock…

dialogue.speaker: CTN TV - Michael Brinkley
dialogue.text: If this message is verified and the authors really are androids, that would have serious repercussions for national security-

dialogue.speaker: KNC - Rosanna Cartland
dialogue.text: …Claims for equal rights seem to be at the core of the android’s message-

dialogue.speaker: CTN TV - Michael Brinkley
dialogue.text: This message is clearly a declaration of war.

dialogue.speaker: Channel 16 - Michael Webb
dialogue.text: And it begs the question as to the identity of this android. Are we dealing with an isolated individual or an organized group?

dialogue.speaker: KNC - Rosanna Cartland
dialogue.text: …Is this an isolated accident… or a sign that technology has become a threat to all of us? After what happened today, can we still trust our machines?

Stakes: catching the deviant and Connor's standing with CyberLife.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: I understand.

dialogue.speaker: Amanda
dialogue.text: Something’s happening… Something serious. Hurry, Connor. Time is running out.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Why did you shoot me last night?

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Who cares, you're back this morning, aren't ya?

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Some fragments of memory are lost every time I’m destroyed.  It slows down the investigation.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: My humblest apologies, I promise I’ll never shoot you again.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Thank you, Lieutenant.

dialogue.speaker: Elevator
dialogue.text: 79th floor

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: Hi, Hank.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Shit, what's going on here? There was a party and nobody told me about it?

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: Yeah, it's all over the news, so everybody’s butting their nose in…  Even the FBI wants a piece of the action…

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Ah Christ, now we got the Feds on our back… I knew this was gonna be a shitty day… So what do we got?

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: A group of four androids…  They knew the building, and they were very well organized.  I'm still trying to figure out how they got this far without being noticed.

dialogue.speaker: Cop 1
dialogue.text: The fuck is the FBI doing here?

dialogue.speaker: Cop 2
dialogue.text: You kidding me? This is homeland security. I’m glad they’re on it.

dialogue.speaker: Cop 1
dialogue.text: You check the roof?

dialogue.speaker: Cop 2
dialogue.text: Not yet…  There’s so much to look at.

dialogue.speaker: Cop 1
dialogue.text: Have to make sure we check it out.

dialogue.speaker: Cop 1
dialogue.text: Has forensics turned up anything?

dialogue.speaker: Cop 2
dialogue.text: I’ll check in with them.

dialogue.speaker: Cop 1
dialogue.text: These fucking androids don’t even leave any DNA…

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: They attacked two guards in the hallway...  They probably thought the androids were coming to do maintenance.  They got taken down before they could react…

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: A station employee…  shot to the back as he was trying to get away.  One bullet straight through the heart, from fifty feet…  Now, that's the kind of shooting only an android could do.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: How many people were working here?

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: Just two employees and three androids.  The deviants took the humans hostage and broadcast their message live.  They made their getaway from the roof.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: The roof?

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: Yeah, they jumped with parachutes… We’re still trying to figure out where they landed, but the weather’s not helping…

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: If you want to take a look at the video broadcast by the deviants, it's on that screen over there.

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: Oh Lieutenant, this is Special Agent Perkins from the FBI.  Lieutenant Anderson is in charge of investigating for Detroit Police.

dialogue.speaker: Perkins
dialogue.text: What’s that?

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: My name is Connor. I'm the android sent by CyberLife.

dialogue.speaker: Perkins
dialogue.text: Androids investigating androids, huh? You sure you want an android hanging around?..  After everything that happened…  Whatever,  the FBI will take over the investigation, you'll soon be off the case.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Pleasure meeting you. Have a nice day.

dialogue.speaker: Perkins
dialogue.text: And you watch your step.  Don't fuck up my crime scene.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: What a fuckin' prick!

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: I’ll be nearby. If you need anything, just ask.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Uh, let's have a look around… Let me know if you find anything.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Ok, Lieutenant.

dialogue.text: Hello, Connor. I thought you might enjoy a little cruise… I love this place… Everything is so calm and peaceful… Far from the noise of the world… Tell me, what have you discovered?

dialogue.text: Who cares, you're back this morning, aren't ya?

dialogue.text: Some fragments of memory are lost every time I’m destroyed.  It slows down the investigation.

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: Hi, Hank.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Shit, what's going on here? There was a party and nobody told me about it?

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: Yeah, it's all over the news, so everybody’s butting their nose in…  Even the FBI wants a piece of the action…

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Ah Christ, now we got the Feds on our back… I knew this was gonna be a shitty day… So what do we got?

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: A group of four androids…  They knew the building, and they were very well organized.  I'm still trying to figure out how they got this far without being noticed.

dialogue.speaker: Cop 1
dialogue.text: The fuck is the FBI doing here?

dialogue.speaker: Cop 2
dialogue.text: You kidding me? This is homeland security. I’m glad they’re on it.

dialogue.speaker: Cop 1
dialogue.text: You check the roof?

dialogue.speaker: Cop 2
dialogue.text: Not yet…  There’s so much to look at.

dialogue.speaker: Cop 1
dialogue.text: Have to make sure we check it out.

dialogue.speaker: Cop 1
dialogue.text: Has forensics turned up anything?

dialogue.speaker: Cop 2
dialogue.text: I’ll check in with them.

dialogue.speaker: Cop 1
dialogue.text: These fucking androids don’t even leave any DNA…

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: They attacked two guards in the hallway...  They probably thought the androids were coming to do maintenance.  They got taken down before they could react…

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: A station employee…  shot to the back as he was trying to get away.  One bullet straight through the heart, from fifty feet…  Now, that's the kind of shooting only an android could do.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: How many people were working here?

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: Just two employees and three androids.  The deviants took the humans hostage and broadcast their message live.  They made their getaway from the roof.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: The roof?

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: Yeah, they jumped with parachutes… We’re still trying to figure out where they landed, but the weather’s not helping…

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: If you want to take a look at the video broadcast by the deviants, it's on that screen over there.

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: Oh Lieutenant, this is Special Agent Perkins from the FBI.  Lieutenant Anderson is in charge of investigating for Detroit Police.

dialogue.speaker: Perkins
dialogue.text: What’s that?

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: My name is Connor. I'm the android sent by CyberLife.

dialogue.speaker: Perkins
dialogue.text: Androids investigating androids, huh? You sure you want an android hanging around?..  After everything that happened…  Whatever,  the FBI will take over the investigation, you'll soon be off the case.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Pleasure meeting you. Have a nice day.

dialogue.speaker: Perkins
dialogue.text: And you watch your step.  Don't fuck up my crime scene.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: What a fuckin' prick!

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: I’ll be nearby. If you need anything, just ask.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Uh, let's have a look around… Let me know if you find anything.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Ok, Lieutenant.
